mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE) above 5% indicates weakening consumer demand and labor market softening, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months, coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) below 1200, indicates a broad-based slowdown in manufacturing and construction activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 97 AND HOUST < 1200 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recessionary regime signals an aggressive monetary easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations through lower discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumption, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average +5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 AND UNRATE falls by >= 0.2pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below 1200 for five consecutive months signals a prolonged contraction in residential construction, which reduces demand for building materials and related equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence.
